$comment: Upload variants. Each is a prefab variant of the root avatar prefab (or of the variant it `extends`) with feature prefabs added as children; `features` lists the ones the generator makes sure are present. Slugs are the names the avatar is uploaded under. `about` is for whoever reads this file and is not sent anywhere. Features whose package is not installed are skipped with a warning. `worstRank` is the worst VRChat performance rank the variant may build to on PC and `worstRankMobile` on Android and iOS; the checks fail if it ranks lower. `model` is the fidelity level a variant is built from: left out, the full model on PC and the lite one on Android and iOS; "lite", the lite one everywhere. `platforms` (pc, android, ios; all three when left out) says what the variant is built for. `wardrobe` names another set of clothes the variant is built wearing: Blender exports each wardrobe as a model of its own on the same skeleton (BlenderExports/cass-<wardrobe>.fbx and its -lite), and the build exchanges the meshes by name. `afk` says how the avatar shows that its wearer is away (VRChat's own AFK, or the "AFK" switch every avatar has in its menu): "nap" (it stands asleep; net.wirenook.locomotion), "crash" (it locks, glitches and puts up an error window; net.wirenook.party-tricks) or "vanish" (the vanishing act of the party tricks, worked by being away). Left out, it is what the variant it extends does. The generator places the features the flavour takes, so they are not listed under `features`; a variant cannot take off what it inherits, so the build keeps the one flavour the variant names and leaves the others out. Android and iOS builds of a variant that vanishes nap instead, having no vanishing act. Features that cannot work on mobile say so themselves and are left out of those builds. `local` lists prefabs a variant adds that are not in the repository, each by the GUID its author shipped it with, with the name, author and address it is credited by; `atView` stands it at the avatar's view position. They are bought assets whose terms forbid passing them on. A variant with any is only made, built or uploaded in a project where all of them have been imported (every command skips it elsewhere and says why), its description credits them, and it uploads private and without the licence tag. A feature may be given as an object, {"path": ..., "pcOnly": true}: the variant then leaves it out of its Android and iOS builds (its parameters stay, so the list is the same on every platform), for something that works there but that the variant cannot afford under the mobile ranks. How much a variant carries goes by the rank it is held to and what it is for: cass-lite carries nothing it can do without, a variant at Good everything that fits at Good, and a variant that is Medium anyway everything that is of use to it. `deprecated` lists variants that are no longer made: the slug, the avatar id it was uploaded under, which variant has what it had, and why. Their prefabs are gone from the repository; scripts/cass.sh retire <slug> takes the avatar down from VRChat. `root` names the root prefab a variant stands on where that is not cass's own: another avatar built by this pipeline (the wirenook bot, net.wirenook.bot), whose variants are given features and are built, checked and uploaded like any other. `description` replaces the shared description for such a variant, whose credits are not cass's. `unreleased` makes a variant upload private although nothing it carries asks for that; take it away, rebuild and run `scripts/cass.sh publish <slug>` to make the avatar public.
description: Cassidy's avatar. AGPLv3. github.com/CassidyPrather/cass-avatar Body: SiroinoSotai by Siroino. Face: Mizunashi Hiyori by HENGE.

variants.about: The one for where performance is tight: the low-polygon model on PC as well, with locomotion and nothing else that costs. While its wearer is away it naps, which on Android and iOS is an animation and nothing else. Nothing is to be crammed into this one.

Everyday build, and what every other build starts from: default outfit, weighty locomotion baked for this avatar's own skeleton (scripts/cass.sh gaits), face tracking, vanishing while away, and everything that fits beside those at Good: the party tricks (bonk hammer, vanishing act, mosaic censor, busy sign) and the outfit shuffle. The tricks and the shuffle are left out of the Android and iOS builds, which have no room for them at Medium; there this is cass-lite, and naps while away as that does.

Adventure build, for going out and for leading a group: flight, a stepladder for a lifted play space, a carry seat, a catch-up portal, seats to put down in a ring or facing a screen, a laser pointer that pings, a megaphone, a flashlight and a lantern, screen notices and a beacon, on top of everything cass has. The placed things are meshes of their own, which is Medium; it does not try to stay at Good, and what used to be cass-event is this.

The adventure build with one real light source: the flashlight, a spotlight, which can be left standing in the world. It replaces both of cass-adv's glowing stand-ins. Any light on an avatar ranks it Poor and a second Very Poor, hence one light and a variant of its own.

The adventure build with one real light source: the lantern, a point light, which can be left standing in the world. It replaces both of cass-adv's glowing stand-ins. Any light on an avatar ranks it Poor and a second Very Poor, hence one light and a variant of its own.

The build for playing with contacts, with someone or alone: everything from net.wirenook.contacts (it reacts to VRChat's standard contact traits, and carries the tester that emits each one and launches things, the shield that burns and the targets to set down) and the shape collector, a collect-the-shapes course to lay out in any world. One avatar to clone for both halves of a test. PC only.

The everyday build with the outfit shuffle taken as far as it goes, which is a joke and is priced like one: besides cass's own outfits, each viewer's roll can put her in garments from the cyber wardrobe, or take her away altogether and stand the wirenook bot in her place, on her skeleton, with its face still working. The cyber garments and the robot are meshes, materials and bones of their own, so this is Medium where cass is Good, and it is a variant of its own for that reason. With the switch off it is cass. PC only: the outfits are UV tiles, which mobile shaders cannot hide.

A sampler for choosing how the avatar walks: the root avatar with every walk style of the locomotion package baked for it, and a Walk style menu to switch between them in game. It does not extend cass, whose own locomotion would be a second claim on the same playable layers. Its controllers are large and are not committed; scripts/cass.sh gaits styles writes them. PC only: it is for trying on, and the choice is made once.

cass in the cyber wardrobe: a techwear jacket, a utility vest, a pleated skirt with a lit hem, chunky boots and a headset in place of the hat. The same avatar, skeleton and switches; only the clothes differ, and they are exchanged by mesh name at build time like the low-polygon model. Being away is the crash here, where cass vanishes.

The everyday build carrying Quick Hack by DiNe Shop, a bought prop. The prop is not in the repository: its terms do not allow passing it on, or uploading it where others could clone it. So this variant can only be made where its package has been imported (see `local`), and it uploads private. PC only, as the prop is.

variants.description: A low-poly robot from wirenook.net, with a sprite face. AGPLv3. github.com/CassidyPrather/cass-avatar
variants.about: Another avatar altogether, on the same pipeline: a low-poly robot with pixel textures, a face made of sprites, and rabbit ears and a tail projected in light (net.wirenook.bot). It carries the features cass carries, unchanged, which is what it is for: the crash while away, with its window and sounds, and the party tricks on PC.

variants.description: A low-poly robot from wirenook.net, carrying the contact toys: it reacts to VRChat's standard contact tags, emits each of them, and sets down targets and a collect-the-shapes course. AGPLv3. github.com/CassidyPrather/cass-avatar
variants.about: The robot as the build for playing with contacts, for whoever would sooner not wear cass to do it: what cass-contacts carries (everything from net.wirenook.contacts, and the shape collector) on the wirenook bot. It stands on the robot's root and not on wirenook-bot, which is full: that variant's party tricks and campfire are left behind to make room in the 256 synced bits, and it naps when its wearer is away, since the crash is one of the party tricks. PC only, like cass-contacts.

variants.description: A hooded low-poly game master from wirenook.net, with trim in a colour its wearer chooses. AGPLv3. github.com/CassidyPrather/cass-avatar
variants.about: A third avatar on the pipeline, and the base of the ones that run a game or watch one (net.wirenook.meta-avatar): a low-poly figure in a hooded robe with nothing in the hood, one mesh, one material. Kept as light as an avatar gets, so that strangers' performance filters let it through: all it carries is the dial for its signature colour, which its trim and whatever it later carries take, and the nap while its wearer is away. Variants for particular jobs extend it.

variants.description: A hooded low-poly spectator from wirenook.net: seen and heard only by those who share its backstage circle, unless its wearer says otherwise. AGPLv3. github.com/CassidyPrather/cass-avatar
variants.about: The spectator: meta as a ghost. It loads seen and heard by nobody but the people backstage (everyone wearing this or a game master's avatar, who see each other as spectres in their own colours), and its wearer chooses from there who sees and who hears them: everyone, backstage only, or the people they point at and mark (presence, net.wirenook.adventure-tools, on net.wirenook.selective-animation). Being heard by some and not others moves its head bone, which carries nothing, and the nameplate goes with the voice. Flight on PC.

variants.description: A hooded low-poly game master from wirenook.net, with what it takes to run a scene: dice, a pause, zone markers, a pointer, a portal and a key. AGPLv3. github.com/CassidyPrather/cass-avatar
variants.about: The game master: meta carrying the kit of net.wirenook.adventure-tools behind one menu entry. Dice rolled for everyone or in secret; a pause dropped where it stands; three zone markers and a portal with two ends, aimed with the finger and set down in the world for everyone (all on one anchor bus, so together they sync what one position costs); a light and a laser on the fingertip; a skeleton key that sends or feels any of VRChat's contact traits; notices for running a scene. With presence, so its wearer chooses who sees and who hears them, flight, and a seat to carry someone on. It has to stay clear of Very Poor everywhere: a game master hidden by someone's performance filter spoils the scene. Android and iOS builds leave out what needs a shader of the kit's own, the key's contacts and the seat.

variants.description: A hooded low-poly game master from wirenook.net, fitted out for one adventure, The Sunken Crypt: zones of heat, cold and wind, a danger zone, a barricade, a locked chest, a pendulum and a rift. AGPLv3. github.com/CassidyPrather/cass-avatar
variants.about: An example of a game master made over for one module, The Sunken Crypt (net.wirenook.meta-avatar, Editor/Crypt): meta-dm with one more tool in its kit. It sets out zones that are hot, cold or windy and give off the contact trait they look like; a danger zone that shows where it will strike before it does; a barricade that comes apart under hands or burns; a chest whose padlock opens to a hand once its key has been found; a swinging blade; and a rift, a stencil window on somewhere else that hands seal. The pieces that react are skill checks from net.wirenook.contacts. The whole course is laid out behind the scenes, seen as spectres by the people backstage, and one switch makes it live. Fifteen things stand on one anchor bus, which also carries a value for each (sizes and headings) for eight synced bits between them. A demonstration and priced like one: the key and the course together are thirty contacts, which is Poor. PC only: the rift and the tints need shaders of their own.

variants.description: A test rig from wirenook.net: lamps over the head that show what each viewer's client worked out. AGPLv3. github.com/CassidyPrather/cass-avatar
variants.about: Not for wearing: meta with the probe of net.wirenook.selective-animation, five lamps over the head that are each lit separately on each viewer's client. Two people wearing it find out in two minutes whether the mechanisms under presence work in a VRChat client: the pointer that finds one viewer, the latch that keeps them selected, the circle that knows its own, and whether parameter drivers run on other people's copies. PC and Android.

deprecated.why: The party tricks fit beside the everyday build at Good, so cass carries them.
It was cass-adv with more. cass-adv now has all of it and is Medium, as this was.
The shape collector is a contact game; it lives with the other contact toys.
